items.headline: Unions stage national protest against Budget
items.summary: Public-sector unions representing teachers, principals, doctors, nurses and other staff marked today as a national protest day against the 2027 Budget. They want a Rs. 25,000 interim allowance, and the nurses' association has warned it may strike.

items.headline: ADB approves $200m for small businesses
items.summary: The Asian Development Bank approved a $200 million package for micro, small and medium enterprises. It combines a policy loan with a credit line that includes $40 million for green lending, and it supports setting up a microfinance regulator.

items.headline: Colombo Port oil spill spreads along coast
items.summary: Containment booms are now in place after marine gas oil leaked from a damaged valve on a port storage tank. The oil has fouled more than 3 km of the Mutuwal coastline, and cleanup is under way with guidance from the Marine Environment Protection Authority.

items.headline: Ex-US envoy flags scrutiny if GSP is renewed
items.summary: Former US ambassador Robert Blake said Sri Lanka could face human-rights scrutiny if the new Democrat-led Congress renews the GSP trade scheme. He urged Colombo to name a new ambassador, repeal the PTA and push ahead with reconciliation.

items.headline: Heavy rain above 75mm forecast in five provinces
items.summary: The Met Department expects heavy showers above 75mm in parts of the Western, Sabaragamuwa, Central, Southern and Uva provinces, as well as in Anuradhapura and Kurunegala districts.

items.headline: Budget committee stage enters day two
items.summary: The committee-stage debate continues today on the votes for the Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism ministries. The final third-reading vote is set for December 14.

items.headline: Indian MP says Jaffna projects are stalled
items.summary: Indian MP Thol. Thirumavalavan claimed Colombo is holding back the India-funded KKS harbour and Jaffna airport upgrades. He said he will take the matter up with India's External Affairs Minister.

items.headline: Review of outdated state websites after DMT hack
items.summary: The Digital Economy Ministry is listing government websites that have not been updated in years. This follows a cyberattack on the Department of Motor Traffic site, which has since been restored, and investigations are continuing.

items.headline: Minister denies diarrhoea claim on tusker's death
items.summary: Environment Minister Dammika Patabendi said he never attributed the death of the elephant Kawanthissa to diarrhoea. Only the post-mortem report can settle the cause, he said, and he asked the newspaper to issue a correction.

items.headline: IRD warns on large cash transactions
items.summary: The Inland Revenue Department warned that cash payments above Rs. 500,000 made outside approved channels may not be deductible for tax. This could raise tax bills on business expenses as well as on land and vehicle deals.

items.headline: Chili importers warned against hoarding
items.summary: The Trade Minister warned importers not to create artificial chili shortages in order to push up prices.

items.headline: Rupee edges up against the dollar
items.summary: The rupee gained slightly against the US dollar in today's trading.

items.headline: Road deaths hit 2,463; festive crackdown planned
items.summary: Police will step up island-wide traffic checks before the holidays, with a focus on drink and drug driving. Road deaths from January 1 to November 21 reached 2,463.

items.headline: Four STF officers hurt as jeep hits train
items.summary: Four Special Task Force officers were injured when their jeep collided with a train at Midigama, near Weligama.

items.headline: Two fishermen killed by train in Trincomalee
items.summary: Two fishermen died after being struck by a train in Trincomalee.

items.headline: Sea mishaps at Mount Lavinia and Hikkaduwa
items.summary: An Indian national drowned at Mount Lavinia beach. In separate incidents, a German tourist and two Russians were rescued from the sea off Hikkaduwa.

items.headline: Probe ordered into mass fish deaths in Kilinochchi
items.summary: A minister ordered an investigation into a large fish die-off at the Kilinochchi tank.

items.headline: Ransilu Jayathilake wins world powerlifting gold
items.summary: The Sri Lankan powerlifter took gold in the 140kg class at the IPL Powerlifting World Championship in Las Vegas.

items.headline: Avish Silva third in UAE karting round
items.summary: The young driver finished third overall in Round 5 of the IAME Bambino Cup in the UAE.

items.headline: Climate summit ends without fossil-fuel deal
items.summary: The global climate talks collapsed after countries could not agree on language about moving away from fossil fuels.

items.headline: 24 killed in Indonesian factory fire
items.summary: Indonesian officials said 24 people died in a factory blaze, and rescuers are still searching for dozens of people who are missing.

items.headline: S. Korea education chief quits over AI cheating
items.summary: South Korea's education minister resigned after a scandal over AI-assisted cheating in university exams.

items.headline: Democrats win largest House majority since 1992
items.summary: US Democrats have won at least 258 House seats, their biggest majority in more than three decades.
